blind_target.title: Look me in the eye: Manipulated eye gaze affects dominance mindsets
blind_target.evidence_quote:
We expected to replicate Carney et al.’s (2010) results when
participants looked directly ahead, such that high-power (vs.
low power) posers report feeling more powerful and take the
gambling risk more often; we also expected these participants
to demonstrate dominance in the ultimatum game (consistent
with Tang & Schmeichel, 2015).
blind_target.outcome_quote:
In sum, holding a direct gaze increased the likelihood of
rejecting a low offer on the hypothetical ultimatum game,
which is consistent with the results of Tang and Schmeichel
(2015). However, we did not find any effects of the pose or
gaze manipulations on the amount of money participants
offered to the opponent or the minimum amount of money participants were willing to accept from the opponent.

shipped_originals.title_o: Effects of potentised substances on growth rate of the water plant Lemna gibba L.

blind_target.evidence_quote: Three series including five independent blinded and randomised experiments each were carried out in the same way as in the original study. Only time and conductor of experiments were modified.
blind_target.outcome_quote: No specific effects of agitated dilutions of gibberellic acid were found in the first two replication series (p=0.263 and p=0.062). In the third serie with gibbous Lemna gibba L. we observed a significant effect (p=0.009) of the homeopathic treatment, however growth was increased in contrast to decreasing in the former study.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The first two series show no original effect and the third shows the opposite direction. The abstract identifies no bibliographic entry for the former study; no target citation is guessed.

shipped_originals.title_o: Beyond Simple Utility: Incentive Design and Trade–Offs for Corporate Employee–Entrepreneurs

blind_target.evidence_quote: In this work, we replicate and extend the study by Monsen et al. (2010) that simultaneously considers financial and non-financial factors as motivators for employee participation in CVs.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Our replication results largely support prior findings and indicate that the extra effort required for participating in a corporate venture is the most important factor driving employees’ decision.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Overall verdict largely supports prior findings; no explicit contrast in available abstract. New extensions are not failures of original results.
